Sir Humphry Davy, chemist and inventor (1778–1829), lived in Italy from 1819–20. S. read Davy’s
Elements of Agricultural Chemistry (1813) in 1820 and made notes on it in Nbk 14. Srumfredevi refers
to one of many mistranscriptions of Davy’s name used by Italians who had only heard but never seen
the chemist’s full name. There is some evidence that Davy enjoyed these approximations — he signed
off letters to an Italian friend ‘Onofrio Davy’ in 1821 and 1825 (see The Collected Letters of Humphry
Davy, eds Tim Fulford and Sharon Ruston (2020) iii 283, 562). Byron socialised with Davy at Ravenna
in spring 1820 (see Byron L&J vii 95), and he is probably S.’s source for this portmanteau of Davy’s
